text:
Nick Cousins scored on what our numbers called a 3% chance, a tip-in at 17:42 of the third period that put Ottawa ahead for the first time since the opening frame, and OTT held on to beat UTA 4-2 at Canadian Tire Centre. Shane Pinto sealed it with an empty-netter 2:02 later. Cousins, drafted 68th overall by the Flyers in 2011 and the game's first star, is not who you'd pick to break a tied game, but the puck found him in front.

The scoreboard flatters Ottawa a little. Utah took 61 shot attempts to 60 and held a 32-21 edge in shots on goal. In expected goals (a measure of chance quality), UTA led 1.21 to 0.63 in the first period, then OTT pulled ahead in the second and again in the third, 1.81 to 0.90. Our simulation of the game's shots gives UTA a slim 51% to 49% edge in who deserved to win. Clayton Keller, the seventh pick in 2016, did his part with a goal, an assist and six shots on goal, and Barrett Hayton tied it at 2-2 with a tip-in at 9:53 of the third.

Goaltending tilted it. Samuel Ersson stopped 30 of 32 shots, about 0.65 goals better than the chances he faced called for, while Karel Vejmelka allowed three on 20 shots, 0.41 worse than expected. Ottawa also scored on one of its two power plays, Fabian Zetterlund's goal in the first, while Utah went 0 for 2. Beyond this game, the facts we have don't give streaks or records for either side, so the result stands as a win Ottawa took late rather than one it controlled.
